analysis_types: linear static impact-equivalent (top plate global bending)
linear static screw pull-through (top plate front stack hole)
linear static frame stack-hole pull-through (local 4 mm model)
linear static frame motor-load (global 4 mm frame)

material.note: PLA screening values; printed layer direction and defects are not measured

top_plate_pull.note: front stack hole, upward pull on top annulus; 4 bottom annuli fixed

top_plate_global.note: 75 g top mass distributed over 35×25 mm; 4 standoff annuli fixed

frame_stack_pull.note: local 4 mm frame model, Ø5 washer; cut boundaries fixed

frame_arm.note: FL motor load; corner values are mesh-dependent at the sharp diamond corner

impact_scenarios.note: 4 screws share the load; a 1 m drop can exceed 1000 g on a hard surface

verdict.top_plate_stack_hole: marginal at ~1000 g without a washer; use Ø5-6 steel washers
verdict.frame_stack_hole: safer than the top plate because the frame is 4 mm thick
verdict.frame_arm_root: the weakest impact location: add fillets/gussets; 50 N motor load is near PLA strength
verdict.top_plate_slots: 1.16 mm edge; reinforce if the battery strap pulls on them

limitations: quasi-static equivalent loads, not transient drop/contact simulations
screw preload, friction and contact are not modelled
isotropic PLA; layer direction and defects are not measured
sharp re-entrant corners produce mesh-dependent stress singularities
a real drop test is required before trusting the safety margin
